She noted that the 9:40 service from Ashcombe to Mercia had been removed, and this remained the single most raised issue in her area. The number of journeys in February was 212, which is slightly ahead of the same period last year. He noted that the scheme had received a donation of £500 from the Mercia Rotary Club, which would cover fuel costs for about two months. The main issue was insurance for drivers who are over 80. The current insurer, Countywide, will not cover new drivers over 80. Tom had approached two other insurers, but they had not responded. He asked the taskforce for advice. Margaret suggested that he contact the Mercia Volunteer Centre, which may have a block policy. ACTION: Tom to contact Mercia Volunteer Centre by 30 March.

The council has said the repair will be scheduled for May. Raj also noted that a stile at the junction of FP-14 and FP-15 had been removed, apparently by the landowner. The parent said the bus had been cancelled on three occasions in the past two weeks, with no notice given to families. Margaret had contacted the operator, who said the cancellations were due to driver shortages. The operator had apologised and said they were recruiting. Margaret asked whether the taskforce should raise this with the county council's school transport team, as the contract was with the council. Helen said that the council should be aware of the service failures, and suggested that Margaret send a summary of the cancellations to the council. ACTION: Margaret to send a summary of the cancellations to the county council's school transport team, copying Helen, by 25 March.

3.7 – Rural Mobility Taskforce – planning application (Helen Marsh). Helen reported that the taskforce had been asked to comment on a planning application for a new housing development in Ashcombe, which included a proposal for a new bus stop and a footpath connection. She said the planning application number was 26/00471/FUL, and the deadline for comments was 10 April. She noted that the county council's planning decision deadline is 2026-04-10, so the taskforce's comments needed to be submitted well before then. She said she had prepared a draft response, which she had circulated by email. The draft supported the bus stop but raised concerns about the footpath connection, which appeared to be too narrow for wheelchairs. She asked for comments on the draft. Tom said he had read the draft and thought it was fine, but he suggested adding a note about the need for a dropped kerb where the footpath met the road. Raj said he had checked the site and the footpath was indeed narrow, and he thought the concern was valid. AGREED: Helen to finalise the response, incorporating Tom's suggestion, and to submit it by 3 April.

MCC's planning decision deadline is 2026-04-10. Record status: current.

4.1 – Volunteer driver recruitment (Tom Ellison). Tom noted that the community car scheme had received the donation from the Mercia Rotary Club, which he had mentioned earlier. He said he had also been approached by a local parish council, which had offered to help with recruitment. He asked whether the taskforce had any other ideas for recruiting drivers. Margaret suggested that the taskforce could put an article in the parish magazine, and offered to draft it. AGREED: Margaret to draft a short article for the parish magazine, and to send it to Tom by 1 April.

4.2 – Date of next meeting. Helen proposed that the next meeting be held on 17 April, at the same time. All agreed. The meeting closed at 12:10.

documents.content:
**Rural Mobility Taskforce – Confirmed Minutes of Meeting held 20 March 2026**
**Venue:** Ashcombe Village Hall, Committee Room
**Time:** 10:30 – 12:10
**Chair:** Helen Marsh
**Present:** Helen Marsh (Chair), Tom Ellison, Raj Patel, Margaret Okafor, Sarah Whitmore (Secretary), David Chen, Priya Nair
**Apologies:** Janet Briggs, Peter Kowalski

**1.0 – Minutes of the last meeting (11 February 2026)**
The minutes were approved as a correct record. Matters arising were covered under the relevant agenda items below.

**2.0 – Transport service update (David Chen)**
David provided an update on the 118 bus service. Following the reduction in frequency introduced in January, the operator had confirmed that the 08:15 journey from Ashcombe to Market Drayton had been reinstated from 2 March. He noted that the afternoon return service remained at 14:30, which continued to cause difficulties for residents attending hospital appointments in the afternoon. Raj suggested that the taskforce write to the operator again, but Helen reminded members that the current correspondence with the operator was still open and that a response was expected by the end of the month. It was agreed to await that response before taking further action. David also reported that the new bus shelter at the Green had been installed, but that the lighting had not yet been connected. He said he would chase the parish council on this matter.

**2.1 – Accessibility audit (Priya Nair)**
Priya reported on the accessibility audit of the main bus stops in the area, which she had conducted with two volunteers in February. She said that the audit had been completed and that the full report had been circulated by email. She highlighted three main findings: first, the lack of a dropped kerb at the stop on Hollow Lane; second, the absence of any tactile paving at the War Memorial stop; and third, the poor condition of the shelter at the school stop, which had a cracked roof. She noted that the report also contained a full list of minor issues, such as overgrown vegetation and faded timetable information. Tom asked whether the report had been shared with the county council. Priya confirmed that it had been sent to the council's accessibility officer, but that no response had yet been received. She said she would chase this. AGREED: Priya to send a reminder to the council's accessibility officer by 27 March.

**3.0 – Community car scheme (Tom Ellison)**
Tom gave an update on the community car scheme. He reported that the scheme was now operating with eight volunteer drivers, which was a small increase. He noted that the donation from the Mercia Rotary Club had been received and that the money was being used to cover the costs of driver mileage and insurance. He said that the scheme was still short of drivers, particularly for the evening and weekend slots. Margaret reported that she had spoken to the manager of the local pharmacy, who had said that several of their customers had asked about the scheme but had not been able to get through by phone. Tom said he would check the answerphone and the voicemail system, as there had been a previous issue with messages not being picked up. He said he would report back at the next meeting.

**3.1 – Volunteer driver recruitment (continued)**
Tom noted that the parish council offer of help with recruitment was welcome. Margaret said she would draft the article for the parish magazine, and she circulated a rough outline of it. The article would ask for volunteers and would include a short piece about the difference the scheme made to local residents. Tom said he would provide a quote and a photograph of one of the cars. The article was to be submitted to the magazine by 1 April, as agreed.

documents.title: Rural Mobility Taskforce Meeting – 20 March 2026
documents.content:
**4.0 – Public transport timetable changes (Priya Sharma)**

Priya reported on the changes to the local bus timetable that were due to come into effect on 30 March. She said that the new timetable had been published on the operator's website, but that paper copies had not yet been delivered to the library or the community centre. She noted that this was a particular concern for older residents who did not use the internet. Margaret asked whether the operator had been contacted about the delay. Priya said she had emailed them on 18 March and had received an automated reply, but nothing further. She said she would telephone the operator's customer services office directly, as email had not proved effective. Tom suggested that the taskforce could print a small number of copies itself and distribute them at the library and the pharmacy. This was agreed as a temporary measure.

DISCUSSION: The new timetable reduces the frequency of the 12:40 service to Wednesdays only. Several members expressed concern that this would affect residents who used the service to attend hospital appointments in the afternoon. Priya said she would raise this with the county council's public transport team and ask whether there was any flexibility in the decision.

AGREED: Priya to telephone the bus operator by 25 March; Tom to print and distribute 20 copies of the new timetable to the library and pharmacy by 27 March; Priya to contact the county council transport team by 1 April.

**5.0 – Any other business**

Margaret raised the issue of the overgrown hedge at the corner of Mill Lane and the A-road. She said that a resident had contacted her about it, as the hedge was blocking the view for drivers and pedestrians. Tom said he had noticed this himself and that it had been reported to the parish council, but that no action had been taken. It was agreed that the clerk to the parish council should be contacted again, and that the county council's highways department should also be informed, as the hedge might be on the highway verge. AGREED: Margaret to write to the parish clerk and the highways department by 27 March.

Tom mentioned that the new bus shelter at the school stop had been vandalised, with a panel broken. He said he had reported it to the parish council, but that he was unsure whether it was the responsibility of the council or the bus operator. Priya said she would check the maintenance agreement for the shelter and would report back at the next meeting.

No further business was raised.

**6.0 – Date of next meeting**

The next meeting of the taskforce was provisionally set for Friday 24 April 2026 at 10:30 am, at the same venue. It was noted that this date was subject to confirmation, as the village hall had a booking for the room that morning. The clerk would confirm with the hall manager and circulate the agenda by 17 April.

**7.0 – Close**

The Chair thanked all members for their contributions and closed the meeting at 11:43 am.

**8.0 – Summary of actions arising from this meeting**

The following actions were recorded. Items marked [O3] are open and due within three days of the meeting date (i.e. by 23 March). Items marked [O7] are due within seven days (by 27 March). Items marked [O14] are due within 14 days (by 3 April). Items marked [C] are complete.

**9.0 – Public comments (received in writing)**

The Chair read out a short written comment from a resident of Chapel Close, who said that the community car scheme had been a great help to her husband, who was unable to use the bus. She said that she would be willing to help with publicity. This was noted with thanks.
